lines: Everything is on the ground and everything stays on the ground. Do not ask me for an exception.
I have grounded this dock four times in nineteen years and all four were named storms.
This one has not got a name. That is precisely why.
Eleven a week. I have flown four in the last fortnight and I did not enjoy any of them.
A pilot can beat into a gale all day. What they cannot do is guess.
Nineteen days of the wind changing its mind is nineteen days of nobody being able to guess.
Three berths, two masts, eleven sailings, and the whole thing hangs on that slate.
Aureline Tuesday and Friday. Crownspire daily. Frostmere when the weather says so.
The weather has always had the last word here. That is not new. It is just louder.
Bookings, manifests, and telling people the thing they do not want to hear.
I am extremely good at the third one and it is the only part anybody remembers.
I took the Frostmere run last week and turned back over the lake. First time ever.
It was not rough. That is what I keep saying and nobody hears it.
It was not rough. It was WRONG. The air was going up where it has never gone up.
Skyreach to Crownspire is ninety minutes and the finest ninety minutes in Averra.
You come off the plateau, the whole crescent opens out, and the sea is there the entire way.
I have done it eleven hundred times and I have never once read a book on it.
Nine tenths of what leaves this dock leaves Caelora entirely. People forget that.
Glass to two regions I have never seen. Spice up from islands with names I say wrong.
Averra is very large and this is a small window in the side of it.
